"import os
import subprocess

clips = [
    {"id": "Clip 1", "start": "01:01:57", "end": "01:02:45"},
    {"id": "Clip 2", "start": "00:50:31", "end": "00:51:30"},
    {"id": "Clip 3", "start": "00:03:29", "end": "00:04:06"},
    {"id": "Clip 4", "start": "00:18:48", "end": "00:19:35"},
    {"id": "Clip 5", "start": "00:42:07", "end": "00:42:55"},
    {"id": "Clip 6", "start": "00:15:28", "end": "00:16:08"}, # Adjusted start time from 15:38 to 15:28 to include the question
    {"id": "Clip 7", "start": "00:26:01", "end": "00:26:29"}
]

ffmpeg_path = r"C:\Users\renu5\Downloads\nishe found\ffmpeg\ffmpeg.exe"
input_video = r"C:\Users\renu5\Downloads\cliping first video\TNE with Louisa Nicola, Keith Rabois episode (1).mp4"
output_dir = r"C:\Users\renu5\Downloads\cliping first video\viral_pipeline"

def time_to_sec(time_str):
    h, m, s = map(int, time_str.split(':'))
    return h * 3600 + m * 60 + s

for clip in clips:
    start_sec = time_to_sec(clip["start"])
    end_sec = time_to_sec(clip["end"])
    duration = end_sec - start_sec
    
    out_video = os.path.join(output_dir, f"{clip['id']}.mp4")
    out_audio = os.path.join(output_dir, f"{clip['id']}.mp3")
    
    print(f"Extracting {clip['id']}...")
    subprocess.run([
        ffmpeg_path, "-y", "-ss", str(start_sec), "-i", input_video, 
        "-t", str(duration), "-c", "copy", out_video
    ], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    
    subprocess.run([
        ffmpeg_path, "-y", "-i", out_video, 
        "-vn", "-c:a", "libmp3lame", "-b:a", "64k", out_audio
    ], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)

print("Extraction complete!")"

def format_time(seconds):
    hours = int(seconds // 3600)
    minutes = int((seconds % 3600) // 60)
    secs = int(seconds % 60)
    millis = int((seconds - int(seconds)) * 1000)
    return f"{hours:02d}:{minutes:02d}:{secs:02d},{millis:03d}"

for clip in clips:
    audio_path = os.path.join(output_dir, f"{clip}.mp3")
    srt_path = os.path.join(output_dir, f"{clip}.srt")
    
    if not os.path.exists(audio_path):
        print(f"Audio not found for {clip}")
        continue
        
    print(f"Transcribing {clip} via Groq...")
    with open(audio_path, "rb") as file:
        transcription = client.audio.transcriptions.create(
            file=(f"{clip}.mp3", file.read()),
            model="whisper-large-v3-turbo",
            response_format="verbose_json",
            timestamp_granularities=["word"]
        )
    
    print(f"Formatting SRT for {clip} (Max 3 words/line)...")
    words = transcription.words
    
    srt_content = ""
    block_index = 1
    
    # Chunk words into groups of max 3
    for i in range(0, len(words), 3):
        chunk = words[i:i+3]
        start_time = chunk[0]['start']
        end_time = chunk[-1]['end']
        text = " ".join([w['word'] for w in chunk])
        
        srt_content += f"{block_index}\n"
        srt_content += f"{format_time(start_time)} --> {format_time(end_time)}\n"
        srt_content += f"{text.strip()}\n\n"
        block_index += 1
        
    with open(srt_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(srt_content)

print("SRT Generation Complete!")
"

"# Landscape (16:9) Video Rendering Plan

Since you want the clips in landscape with the captions burned in, I will create a new automated pipeline to generate these files so they are 100% ready for Twitter.

## Proposed Changes

    subtitle_path = f"9x16/{clip_name}.srt"
    output_video = os.path.join("16x9", f"{clip_name}.mp4")
    
    if not os.path.exists(input_video):
        print(f"Skipping {clip_name}: Input video not found")
        continue
    
    if not os.path.exists(os.path.normpath(subtitle_path)):

        output_video
    ]
    
    try:

        print(f"Successfully generated {output_video}")
